Figure 2:Motivation and intuition.Left: image editors handle complex edits such as actions and relighting on single frames, whereas video editors lack the paired data to learn them. Our goal is a video editor that makes these edits while keeping the video temporally consistent.
Middle: can a video editor learn to edit images by treating each image as a one-frame video? Right: video editing ability improves while temporal quality remains comparable.

Figure 3:I2VT and the offline distillation baseline.Left: offline distillation fine-tunes on teacher-edited images. Middle: I2VT supervises the student along its own rollout. The cross marks stop-gradient.
Right: at inference, the student edits whole video clips.
Figure 4:Editing tasks in OpenVE++.Source frames and instructions illustrate the four task groups evaluated across 207 clips.

Figure 5:Offline versus online distillation with I2VT.Bernini-R-1.3B on a basic edit from OpenVE-Bench (left) and a body-movement edit from OpenVE++ (right), showing three frames sampled from each video.

Figure 6:Qualitative results.Top and middle rows show new and basic edits, comparing the source, base editor, and I2VT. The bottom row compares I2VT-1.3B with other editors on OpenVE++ action and expression edits. Each video shows two frames at matched times.

Figure S1:Released GokuSubject Movementpairs.Top: the target lowers the hand, and the lips that move in the source stay still in the target. Bottom: the target turns the torso and performs a different dance.

Figure S2:Transformer block of the student editors.A rank-128 LoRA trains the linear layers marked with a flame. The block repeats 30 times in Bernini-R-1.3B, 40 times per expert in Bernini-R-14B, and 40 times in VideoCoF.
Figure S3:A new-task training example from I2VT-17K.We check a source frame before assigning it a body-movement edit and then pair it with instructions for the image and video editors.
Figure S4:Teacher guidance for offline distillation targets.JoyAI-Image-Edit edits training frames at guidance11,22, and55. Instructions are abridged.

Figure S5:New abilities on OpenVE++(Bernini-R-1.3B). Each example shows three frames of the source, the base editor, and the student trained with I2VT. Asked to lower the woman’s head (top left), the base editor adds a cap, and asked to raise the man’s arm (top middle), it adds another person’s arm.

Figure S6:I2VT-CoF on OpenVE-Bench and OpenVE++.Each example shows three source frames (left) and the edited frames (right). The bottom row shows one OpenVE++ edit from each new task group. Instructions are abridged.
